byo-subscription.rationale: Kepler uses the users own coding-agent sign-ins and reads supported plan usage through that native account. It adds no markup on the agents brought to Kepler. Grok Build accepts an xAI API key, and Pi reads its own provider-key environment variables. These are agent-specific routes, not a Kepler token bundle. A GitKraken account is required for the public-preview application. Experimental Automations also explicitly require sign-in.

review.note: Independently checked this exact typed value, eligible atomic finding, cited pinned evidence, client/release scope and dates. This is separate from factual claim acceptance.

local.rationale: Local mode runs work on the current execution computer. Remote environments run the core/agents on an accessible user-owned SSH machine or WSL instance, with setup performed by Kepler. Disconnect closes the current window connection only; the remote server keeps its agent sessions running. Remote Access to a local laptop does not move execution off that laptop.

The worktree mechanism separates Git checkouts. No hostile-code containment follows from that file boundary or from configuring a remote host.

issue-tracking.rationale: Kepler owns persistent tasks with prompt/notes, worktrees, linked issues/PRs and multiple agent sessions. task_create creates a separate task without starting it. Tasks carry stage/hold/archive state, which the task tools can read or change separately from session state. Tasks can begin with no external issue or repository, so a connected issue tracker is optional for this task workflow.
